solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Working daily? In theory

definitions.meaning: someone employed on a daily newspaper works on a printed sheet
something true in principle but not yet in practice holds as written down

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both employed by a newspaper and true only in principle, not proven in practice.

clue.text: Port does as rum

indicators.note: rum is an old word for odd or strange, so the letters are put in a strange order

explanation.surface: A harbour behaves just like a spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Odessa is a major Black Sea port in Ukraine.

clue.text: March past a row of shops

definitions.meaning: a ceremonial procession of troops marching
a line of shops, as in a shopping arcade

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a ceremonial procession and also a street of shops.

clue.text: Intercede on someone's behalf? You may already have, here!

definitions.meaning: to speak up for someone to help them
a solver filling a crossword grid has written words into it already

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means recommending someone, and literally inserting a word as in a grid.

clue.text: Check about special synthetic substance

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain

explanation.surface: Inspecting an unusual man-made material.
explanation.definitionFit: Resins include synthetic polymers used in plastics and adhesives.

clue.text: Jotter found in flat next to record

indicators.note: next to places one piece beside the other in the charade

parts.note: to note something is to record it
a pad is slang for a flat or apartment

explanation.surface: A notebook turns up in somebody's apartment beside a vinyl record.
explanation.definitionFit: A jotter is a small notebook for quick notes, the same as a writing pad.

clue.text: Second in command, without feeling, wrote off

parts.note: numb means lacking sensation

indicators.note: off means gone bad or awry, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A deputy, emotionally dead, writes something off.
explanation.definitionFit: A number two is a deputy, the person second in charge.

clue.text: Grass in furrow around front of field

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a rut is a groove or furrow

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Grass grows in a ploughed furrow at the edge of a field.
explanation.definitionFit: Turf is grass with the soil held by its roots.

clue.text: Eternal child's favourite — parent endlessly liberal

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

indicators.note: liberal means free, so the letters are freely rearranged
endlessly means the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A child's favourite parent is endlessly permissive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts PARENT to PAREN, and 'liberal' makes that ERPAN; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Pan is J M Barrie's boy who never grows up, an eternal child.

clue.text: Amazing Sudanese ballerina

indicators.note: amazing suggests something astonishingly transformed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remarkable dancer from Sudan.
explanation.definitionFit: A danseuse is a female ballet dancer, the French word used in English.

clue.text: Heron, say, on far side of moat

parts.note: say introduces an example, abbreviated e.g.
on in the sense of concerning, as in re

indicators.note: the far side of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A heron stands on the opposite bank of a castle's moat.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a kind of heron, a white wading bird.

clue.text: Voluntary worker at marina's injured

indicators.note: injured means damaged, so the letters are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: A volunteer is hurt at a yacht marina.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's counts as an S here: AT MARINAS is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A Samaritan is a volunteer helper, especially with the British Samaritans charity, which listens to people in distress.

clue.text: Team triumph, the German air-to-air missile

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
to win is to triumph
der is the German word for the

explanation.surface: A football side's victory leads to a German missile.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sidewinder is a well-known American heat-seeking air-to-air missile.

clue.text: Exempt from toll crossing river

indicators.note: crossing means the toll spans the river, holding it within

parts.note: a toll is a fee charged for passage

explanation.surface: No charge is made for a bridge over the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link: 'Exempt from' reads as one phrase, but the toll is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Free means not required to pay, exempt from a charge.

clue.text: Stifling son by being over-protective?

parts.note: mothering means fussing protectively over someone

explanation.surface: Smothering one's boy with too much care.
explanation.definitionFit: Smothering means suffocating or stifling.

clue.text: Tommy intends realising money from investments

parts.note: Tommy is the nickname for a British private soldier
to mean to do something is to intend it

explanation.surface: A soldier plans to earn money from shares.
explanation.definitionFit: Private means is income from investments or inheritance rather than from work.

clue.text: Watchman unhappy living at top of esplanade

indicators.note: unhappy suggests something upset, so the letters are disturbed
the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

explanation.surface: A miserable guard living at the head of the promenade.
explanation.definitionFit: A vigilante watches and acts as a self-appointed guardian of law and order.

clue.text: Champion eight reportedly unhappy about capsizing

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so a word with the same sound is used

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen
sad means unhappy

indicators.note: capsizing means turning over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A star rower is upset when the boat overturns.
explanation.walkthrough: CREW said aloud gives CRU, the French word for a wine growth; 'capsizing' turns RE into ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusader is a champion of a cause.

clue.text: Steals bits

definitions.meaning: a snaffle is a simple jointed mouthpiece in a horse's bridle

explanation.definitionFit: The word means pinches or takes, and also simple bridle bits for horses.

clue.text: Candidate's expenses on the road?

parts.note: a candidate standing for office is running, and a car's upkeep on the road is its expense of operation

explanation.surface: An election hopeful's travel bills while out campaigning.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the cost of operating a vehicle, and puns on a candidate who runs for office.

clue.text: Provided rolls and assortment of teas for carnival

indicators.note: rolls means turns over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: if means provided that

indicators.note: an assortment is a mixture, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Bread rolls and various teas laid on for a festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolls' turns IF into FI; 'assortment of' turns TEAS into ESTA.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiesta is a festival or carnival, from the Spanish.

clue.text: Tranquil piece of music a duke brought out

indicators.note: brought out means removed, so these letters leave the word

parts.note: a serenade is a piece of music, often played at evening

explanation.surface: A calm piece of music is performed by a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Serene means calm and peaceful, tranquil.

clue.text: Separate if seen in street

indicators.note: seen in places the little word inside the abbreviation

explanation.surface: Telling whether something is spotted in a road.
explanation.definitionFit: To sift is to separate, as grain from chaff through a sieve.

clue.text: Completely tie them in knots, continuously

parts.note: all means wholly, completely

indicators.note: tied in knots means twisted about, so the letters are tangled

explanation.surface: Somebody keeps tying people up in knots without a break.
explanation.definitionFit: Constantly and without stopping, the idiom means continuously.

clue.text: Runs into nurse in a rage

indicators.note: into places one piece inside the other

parts.note: to tend is to nurse or care for
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone bumps into a furious nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link; 'a rage' is the definition, a fashion that is all the rage.
explanation.definitionFit: A trend is a craze, something all the rage.

clue.text: Elderly housed in Swanage, Dorset

indicators.note: housed in means the letters are lodged inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Old people living in a Dorset seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Swanage is a seaside town in the English county of Dorset.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words describe a person who has lived many years and reached old age.

clue.text: Coach shows dedication

definitions.meaning: steady hard-working application to a task

explanation.definitionFit: The word means careful persistent effort, and historically a French stagecoach.

clue.text: Take legal action following one's publication

indicators.note: following places the legal action after the one's

parts.note: one is I, and one's gives I'S, read as IS
to sue is to take legal action

explanation.surface: A lawsuit comes after someone's article appears in print.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue is one edition of a magazine or newspaper, a publication.

clue.text: Form of rise appropriate for the remainder

indicators.note: a form of a word is that word reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: due means fitting or appropriate

explanation.surface: A kind of increase suits the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Residue is what is left over, a remainder.

clue.text: Lower degrees read badly

parts.note: deg is the abbreviation for degrees

indicators.note: badly means poorly done, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Weaker degree results read out poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: To degrade is to lower in status, rank or quality.
